subject: general
question: Which of the following is a correct order of basicity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CsOH > KOH > NaOH > LiOH**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The basicity of alkali metal hydroxides increases as we move down the group in the periodic table.
 
• This is because the ionic nature and size of the cation increase as we move down the group.
 
• CsOH is the most basic among the given hydroxides because cesium is at the bottom of the alkali metal group.
 
• LiOH is the least basic because lithium is at the top of the alkali metal group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basicity:**

 
 
• Basicity refers to the ability of a substance to accept protons (H+ ions) or donate a pair of valence electrons to form a bond.
 
• In the context of alkali metal hydroxides, basicity is determined by the extent to which the hydroxide ion (OH-) is available to react with acids.
 
 
 
• **Alkali Metal Hydroxides:**
 
 
• Alkali metal hydroxides are compounds formed by alkali metals (Group 1 elements) and hydroxide ions (OH-).
 
• Examples include LiOH (Lithium Hydroxide), NaOH (Sodium Hydroxide), KOH (Potassium Hydroxide), and CsOH (Cesium Hydroxide).
 
• These hydroxides are strong bases and are highly soluble in water.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table Trends:**
 
 
• As we move down Group 1 in the periodic table, the size of the alkali metal cations increases.
 
• This leads to a decrease in the lattice energy of the hydroxides, making them more soluble and hence more basic.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Nature:**
 
 
• The ionic nature of a compound refers to the extent to which it dissociates into ions in a solution.
 
• Alkali metal hydroxides dissociate completely in water, releasing hydroxide ions, which contribute to their basicity.
